movie.title: Once Upon a Time in the Middle East
movie.overview: Xu Fu travels to the Middle East to work as a chef in a Chinese restaurant to pay off family debts, where he meets floor manager Ma Junsheng. Their Dragon Restaurant rises to fame, attracting crowds with authentic‑tasting Chinese food. But war breaks out, and local conditions take a drastic turn for the worse. No one can remain unaffected. What lies ahead for them? And how will the Dragon Restaurant hold on amid the war?

reviews.author: tomaslisheng
reviews.content:
I went into *Welcome to Dragon Restaurant* expecting another Shen Teng comedy — and walked out with my eyes swollen from crying. It far exceeded every expectation; this is not a comedy at all, but one of the most powerful anti-war films I've ever seen.  
Director Wen Muye never relies on spectacle or bloodshed to condemn war. Instead, he exposes its cruelty through contrast: a humble Chinese kitchen planted in the middle of a war zone, where a sizzling wok and a bowl of hot rice become the quietest, most devastating protest against violence. Shen Teng, as chef Xu Fu, sheds his comic persona and delivers a heartbreaking performance — every shared meal becomes a small act of resistance, a stubborn insistence that life, dignity, and peace still matter amid the ruins.  
 Bring tissues — a lot of them if you are going to watch it

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When war erupts in the Middle East, a Chinese chef and a floor manager struggle to keep their famed restaurant alive amidst rising chaos.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Hoping to pay off mounting family debts, Xu Fu travels to the Middle East to work as a chef in a Chinese restaurant alongside floor manager Ma Junsheng. Together, they transform the Dragon Restaurant into a wildly popular culinary destination known for its authentic Chinese cuisine. However, their newfound success is shattered when war breaks out across the region, drastically altering local conditions. As conflict engulfs everything around them, the duo must fight to survive and preserve their sanctuary.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Driven by severe financial strain back home, Xu Fu leaves China for the Middle East, securing employment as a chef at a modest Chinese eatery. There, he partners with Ma Junsheng, a sharp and diligent floor manager who oversees the establishment's daily operations. Through Xu Fu's exceptional culinary skills and Ma Junsheng's effective management, the Dragon Restaurant becomes a resounding success, attracting eager crowds hungry for traditional dishes. The restaurant quickly evolves into a vibrant cultural hub and a source of stability for both men and their community. However, this peaceful period comes to an abrupt end when armed conflict erupts in the region, plunging the surrounding area into violence and uncertainty. As the local political landscape worsens, daily life becomes increasingly dangerous, forcing the duo to navigate severe resource shortages and constant threats to their safety. No longer isolated from the harsh reality of war, Xu Fu and Ma Junsheng must make difficult choices to protect their staff and patrons. Ultimately, the story highlights their resilience, brotherhood, and determination to maintain a sense of home and humanity in a region torn apart by conflict.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Once Upon a Time in the Middle East follows Xu Fu, a determined Chinese chef who moves to the region to work in a local restaurant and relieve his family's heavy debts. Partnering with efficient floor manager Ma Junsheng, Xu Fu turns the Dragon Restaurant into a thriving haven celebrated for its authentic Chinese food. Their prosperous journey takes a dramatic turn when war erupts, trapping the restaurant and its staff in the midst of violent turmoil. The narrative explores the perseverance, unity, and survival of ordinary individuals fighting to maintain hope and shelter amidst harrowing circumstances.
